findings.title: After a trap's victim has rolled and noticed it, the tracker still says it waits for that roll and offers to ask for it again
findings.control: Ask for the opening roll again (and the tracker's state line)
findings.what_happens: A trap's opening is the victim's roll. On a success resolveVictimOpening tells the GMs and returns without writing the stage (murder-rules.mjs:861-890), so the incident stays at openingRoll until a GM ends it, as DRPG.Murder.victimNoticedNext says. The tracker reads the stage alone: its bar goes on saying 'Opening - waiting for {victim}'s opening roll' (murder-ui.mjs:463-471) and its footer still draws Ask for the opening roll again (627-629). A press sends a new invitation and the toast says it was offered. With the victim's player connected the primary's draw refuses that roll as thrown already (roll-draw.mjs:1154-1155), the window re-offers itself to the third try (murder-rules.mjs:4666-4685) and the GMs are then told the player did not make the opening roll (4695-4701). With the player away the GM throws it here and resolveOpening has no once-only check (4730-4746), so the trap is rolled a second time.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM opens a trap, the victim's player rolls 20 or more and notices it; the GM looks at the tracker, reads that it waits for the opening roll, presses Ask for the opening roll again, and the player gets three roll windows that are each refused, after which the GMs' chat says the player did not make the roll.
findings.expected: Once the opening is scored the tracker says so (the trap was noticed; end it when the scene is done) and offers no second opening roll.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for anything that marks a scored opening: resolveVictimOpening's success branch writes no state, and git grep finds no field for it (trapNoticed, noticedAt, openingDone: none). Read whether the bar or the footer read more than the stage: they do not. Looked for a once-only rule: resolveOpening has none, the primary's draw has one for a player's roll. No test or scenario reads the tracker after a noticed trap (git grep victimNoticed, reask, openingReask in scripts/tests-*.mjs and audit/harness/scenarios: none). The comment at murder-rules.mjs:884-888 says leaving the stage is deliberate; it says nothing of the tracker's line or of this button.
findings.probe: As GM: game.drpg.murderDialog(), tick A trap, Open the incident; let the victim's page throw a success; then read the tracker's .drpg-turn-bar and press footer button[data-action=reask]; read the victim's page (roll windows, notices) and the GMs' whispers.

findings.title: A death by the student's own hand has no 'Ask for the opening roll again', though the GMs' notice tells them to press it
findings.control: Ask for the opening roll again
findings.what_happens: One student in both seats still opens on Stage 4's roll, thrown by that student's player and re-offered up to three times (murder-rules.mjs:4661-4685). When it is not made, the GMs are whispered DRPG.Murder.openingDeclined: 'Press Ask for the opening roll again on the Incident tracker, or end the incident.' The tracker's footer draws that button only when the incident is not selfInflicted (murder-ui.mjs:627-629), so for this incident it shows End the murder and Close alone under a bar that says it waits for the roll. reaskOpening and rollOpening themselves would work for it (663-676, 4426-4450); the condition came in with the button (commit 5c66ffab, 12.09.2026), whose note gives a reason for no Pass in such a death and none for no re-ask.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM opens a murder with one student as killer and victim, the player closes the roll window three times (or was away and the GM closed its own), the chat tells the GMs to press Ask for the opening roll again, and the tracker has no such button: the one road left is End the murder and opening it again.
findings.expected: The button the notice names is on the tracker for this incident too, or the notice names what is there.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for another road that sends the roll again: reaskOpening is called from the tracker alone and rollOpening from openMurder and reaskOpening (git grep). Read rollOpening and throwOpeningRoll for a refusal of a self-inflicted incident: none. Read the comment above the condition (murder-ui.mjs:616-626) and the commit that added it: no decision of the owner is named for leaving the re-ask out.
findings.probe: As GM open the murder window with one student in both lists and Open the incident; on that student's page close the roll window three times; read the GMs' whisper, then the tracker's footer: button[data-action=reask] is absent.

findings.title: With 'Keep character sheets anonymous' off nothing opens Take from the Body
findings.surface: A dead student's sheet as another player reads it
findings.what_happens: The window's one opener is the button buildBodyLoot draws on a body's sheet (anonymity.mjs:299-309), and buildBodyLoot is called at one place, the end of the redaction (144). The render hook returns before it when the world's switch is off (127). So in a world with the switch off a player who opens a dead student's sheet reads it whole, with no list 'What they were carrying' and no button, and no other control calls openBodyLoot or requestBodyLoot (git grep: anonymity.mjs alone). Both handbooks tell the player to open the sheet and press Take from the Body with no word of the switch (gm-handbook.en.md:935, player-handbook.en.md:857), and the anonymity audit's line for the switch (DRPG.Anonymity.audit.switchOff) says only that the sheets are read whole.
findings.failure_scenario: At a table that turned the switch off in the module's settings, a student stands over a body, opens its sheet and finds no Take from the Body anywhere; the body cannot be searched by a player.
findings.expected: The button is on a body's sheet whether or not the sheet is redacted, or the switch's hint and the audit say that Take from the Body goes with it.
findings.refutation_tried: git grep openBodyLoot, buildBodyLoot, DRPG.Loot.open and requestBodyLoot in scripts: one opener, one caller of it, both behind the return at 127. Read sheet-mode.mjs for another viewer's road (rows are the editor's alone). Read the setting's hint (lang/en.json:287-288), the audit's lines and both handbooks for a word that ties Take from the Body to the switch: only closed sheets are said to stop it (DRPG.Anonymity.audit.closed). The only test that turns the switch off (tier 2 E20-T1) reads the audit, not a body.
findings.probe: On the GM: game.settings.set('danganronpa-rpg', 'enforceAnonymity', false), a student dead and public, its sheet at Observer. On a player's page open that sheet: document.querySelector('.drpg-loot-open') is null; with the switch on it is the button.

findings.title: The re-ask's toast says the opening roll was offered before anything is, and when nothing is
findings.control: Ask for the opening roll again
findings.what_happens: reaskOpening starts rollOpening without waiting and says 'The opening roll was offered again: to the victim of a trap, otherwise to the killer.' in the same step (murder-ui.mjs:671-673). rollOpening first needs the opening's statistic: when the incident holds none (a betrayal's, whose statistic window the GM closed) it opens the GM's own window and sends nothing until that is answered, sends nothing at all if the window is closed or already open (murder-rules.mjs:4484-4499), and with the roller's player away it throws the roll on this GM's browser (4449).
findings.failure_scenario: A GM who closed the statistic window of a betrayal's opening presses Ask for the opening roll again: the toast says the roll was offered while the GM's own statistic window opens, and closing that window offers it to nobody.
findings.expected: The toast follows what rollOpening did: offered to a player, thrown here, or waiting for the GM's pick.
findings.refutation_tried: Read rollOpening's three ends (asked, thrown here, null) and that reaskOpening reads none of them. An incident opened from the murder window carries its statistic (murder-ui.mjs:315), so there the toast is only early by the socket's send.
findings.probe: As GM let a betrayal open (or call openMurder with no openingTrait), close the statistic window, then press button[data-action=reask] on the tracker and read the notices and which windows open.

findings.title: A second discovery that reaches its two witnesses while the prompt of the first is open is never asked of the GM
findings.surface: The prompt for a discovery waiting for the GM's word
findings.what_happens: When a walk reaches the count the room's row is written and askPendingBodies is called (body.mjs:852-855). One prompt runs at a time: a call while one is open answers that prompt's promise (908-912). promptPendingBodies read its rows once, before the first window (917), and asks those alone (922), so a row written while the GM is looking at the first window is in no loop, and nothing asks again when the first is answered. A later walk into the second room asks nothing either, because its row stands (849-851). What is left is the note in the Body found window (1180-1182), the GM panel's Next line (gm-panel.mjs:949-950) and the next reload or GM leaving (956-962).
findings.failure_scenario: Two bodies lie in two rooms; two students walk in on the first and the GM's prompt opens; before the GM answers, two others walk in on the second: its finders hear the sound and are told privately, and the GM is never prompted about it.
findings.expected: Every discovery that reaches its count is asked once, the second after the first is answered.
findings.refutation_tried: Read every caller of askPendingBodies (body.mjs:855, 958, 961): a walk that reaches the count, the GM stores opening, a GM leaving. Read promptPendingBodies for a second read of the rows: none. The walk that would ask again is stopped by the standing row. The owner's decision A (13.11.2026) is that the GM is asked; nothing found decides this case. No test walks two rooms while a prompt is open (R5741 and scenario 10 use one room).
findings.probe: On the primary GM with two kept bodies in two rooms: walk two students into the first room and leave the prompt open; walk two others into the second; answer the first prompt; read that no second 'Students found a body' window opens while pendingBodyDiscoveries() still lists the second room.

findings.title: The checklist's first button, Body found, is drawn on a GM whose press is always refused
findings.surface: The checklist after an incident that left a body
findings.what_happens: Any GM may end a murder from the tracker, and the checklist opens on that GM's browser (murder-rules.mjs:3664-3670). Its primary button, the one Enter presses, opens the body's announcement, which only the primary GM's browser makes: on another GM openBodyDiscoveryDialog answers with the notice 'Only the primary GM, {name}, can announce a body...' and opens nothing (body.mjs:1107, 176-181). The checklist has closed with the press, and the primary GM was shown no checklist.
findings.failure_scenario: At a table with two GMs the second ends the murder on their tracker, presses Enter on the checklist and reads that only the first GM can announce a body; the autopsy and the Investigation buttons went with the window.
findings.expected: On a GM who cannot announce, the button is shut with that reason, or the checklist is the primary GM's.
findings.refutation_tried: The refusal is told and names who can, and tier 2 holds it ('a GM who is not the primary announces no body and is told whose it is'), so this is the button's audience, not a silent failure. Read afterIncident for a look at who the primary is before it draws the footer: none.
findings.probe: With two GMs connected, on the one that is not the primary: open and end a murder that left a body from the tracker, then press button[data-action=body] on 'After the incident'.

findings.title: Silence now on the tracker is decided when the window opens and does not follow the victim's death or its publication
findings.what_happens: Whether the footer carries Silence now is read once, as openIncidentTracker starts (murder-ui.mjs:703). The body of the window is rebuilt live, but the footer is redrawn only by a reopen, and the tracker reopens itself only when the stage or selfInflicted changes (584-586, 762-763). So a victim marked dead under an unchanged stage (Kill in the Students window or game.drpg.deathDialog(), with Stage 6 declined) gets no button until the tracker is closed and opened again; and a button drawn before the body was announced, or before another GM pressed it, stays, and its press writes nothing and says nothing (silenceDeadNow answers false, incident-store.mjs:982) before the tracker reopens without it. The Students window's own Silence now follows the deaths live (gm-students.mjs:575).
findings.failure_scenario: During a fight, with the tracker open, the victim is marked dead with Kill in the Students window (the GM panel is back by finding 8, or a second GM does it) and Stage 6 is answered Cancel; the tracker on screen does not offer Silence now for the body until it is closed and opened again.
findings.expected: The button follows the victim's death, its publication and the cast's silencedDead while the tracker stands open.
findings.refutation_tried: Read keepLive (live.mjs:106-204): it replaces the region, never the footer. Read what the tracker watches (759): actors, tokens, the incident's setting and the cast's hook, none of which redraws a footer. In the ordinary close of a fight the stage moves first and the death is recorded after it (murder-rules.mjs:2880-2904, 2434-2452), so the reopen and the death race; which lands first at a table was not established (see not_established).
findings.probe: Open a direct murder, let the fight start, leave the tracker open; mark the victim dead with game.drpg.deathDialog and answer Cancel to 'The incident's victim died'; read the tracker's footer for button[data-action=silence].

findings.title: The GM panel comes back over a running incident the first time the tracker reopens itself (window flow, not a control's look)
findings.control: the tracker's own reopen at a stage change (no control)
findings.what_happens: The GM panel closes for a tile and opens again when the tile's run() settles (gm-panel.mjs:605-618). The Murder tile's run is openMurderDialog, which awaits the tracker so that, as its note says, the panel is not dropped on a live incident (murder-ui.mjs:341-349). But when the stage changes under an open tracker - the opening roll lands, in every murder - the tracker closes itself and opens a new one from a then() nobody awaits (769-770). The close settles the first tracker's wait, openMurderDialog returns true, and the GM panel opens beside the new tracker as the fight begins. No verdict of the list names this exactly; it is filed under stale-state because the panel's return no longer follows the tracker's life.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM opens a murder from the GM panel; the killer's opening roll succeeds; the tracker redraws for the fight and the GM panel pops open over it.
findings.expected: The panel stays away while a tracker of that incident stands, as the note at murder-ui.mjs:341-343 intends.
findings.refutation_tried: Read openGmPanel for a look at a running incident: none (gm-panel.mjs:533-545). Read whether the reopen is chained to the first tracker's promise: it is not (the then() is on dialog.close()). Pass, Silence now and the re-ask do return the next tracker (murder-ui.mjs:781, 785, 789), so those keep the chain.
findings.probe: From the GM panel press the Murder tile, Open the incident, and let the killer's page roll a success; read which windows stand on the GM: .drpg-window-incident and .drpg-window-panel together.

findings.title: End the murder's question does not say that, for a death by the student's own hand, the yes records the death
findings.surface: The question 'End the murder' asked from the tracker
findings.what_happens: The question has one sentence for every incident: 'Stop tracking this murder? Lost Health and Sanity, items, and Remnants stay as they are.' For an incident by the student's own hand at Stage 6, closing it is the moment the student is killed (murder-rules.mjs:3473-3477), kept by the GMs until the body is found. The GMs were told so on the card that opened Stage 6 (DRPG.Murder.resolutionNoteSelf) and the handbook says it; the button's own question, written by the rule that a yes says what it does (murder-ui.mjs:792), does not.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM who opened a death by the student's own hand by mistake presses End the murder at Stage 6 to drop it, reads 'Stop tracking this murder?', confirms, and the student is dead.
findings.expected: For this incident the question says that ending it records the death.
findings.refutation_tried: Read the whisper at Stage 6 (murder-rules.mjs:741), the opening's card (DRPG.Murder.openedSelfNote) and gm-handbook.en.md:1122: each says the death is recorded at the close, so the GM has been told elsewhere; the finding is the question's own words. reviveCharacter can take the death back.
findings.probe: Open the murder window with one student in both lists, let the roll succeed, press End the murder on the tracker and read the question's body before answering.

findings.title: Details in the Direct Murder declaration's confirmation does nothing
findings.surface: The Direct Murder declaration in an Eclipse
findings.what_happens: The confirmation a player gets for a Direct Murder in an Eclipse puts the action's briefing in its body (action-murder.mjs:327). briefingBlock always ends in the Details toggle and its box (action-briefing.mjs:100). The toggle's listener is added by wireDetails, which only action-menus.mjs actionWindow calls (309); this window is ui-kit.mjs drpgConfirm, whose frame wires steppers, mode bars and scroll signals and nothing else (ui-kit.mjs:1026-1041). So the button is drawn with its tooltip 'Shows or hides the price, the rolls, and what each result does' and a press does nothing: the box stays shut, as it is by default (settings.mjs:1686-1691), and the lines in it - 'Costs 1 action. You have N.' and the room - cannot be read there. The 16 other call sites of briefingBlock hand it to chooseVariant or actionWindow (the brief: sites and the Dynamic action's read one by one; the intro: sites by their shape).
findings.failure_scenario: In an Eclipse a player presses Direct Murder, reads the confirmation, presses Details to see the price and nothing happens.
findings.expected: The toggle opens and shuts its box here as in every action window, or this confirmation draws no toggle.
findings.refutation_tried: git grep wireDetails and drpg-action-details in scripts: one definition, one caller (actionWindow's render); a11y.mjs only reads such toggles and notice-history.mjs only lists the class. Read wireKit and dressFrame for a generic wiring of aria-expanded buttons: none. R3382 and R3200 hold the Details of the action windows' list, and this confirmation is not on that list (tests-tier0.mjs:23806). The sentence's window that follows is an actionWindow (action-menus.mjs:522), so its own Details works.
findings.probe: On a player's page in an Eclipse press the sheet's Direct Murder tile; in the confirmation click .drpg-action-details-toggle and read its aria-expanded and whether .drpg-action-details-box loses inert.

not_established: Nothing was pressed or run in this pass: every row is label -> element -> listener -> handler -> effect read in the source at b5a29e73, with the tests and scenarios that press or pin it named where git grep found them.

Whether Foundry 14's DialogV2 keeps the <form> a window's body brings (utils.mjs dialogContent hands it a bare div). The callbacks read here find their fields either way, by reading: d.element.querySelector('form') then answers DialogV2's own form, which holds the same named fields (the murder window's killer, victim, indirect and openingTrait; the body's room and victim; the death's actor, keepBullets and secret). Not compared with a drawn v14 window.

Announce the body and Record the death open disabled: the kit writes the button's disabled itself (ui-kit.mjs:297-299) and death.mjs chooseFirst lifts it on a choice. Foundry 14's own drawing of a disabled dialog button, and whether a press of one is refused by Foundry, were not read; tier 2 E22-T1 presses Enter in both windows on the harness's model.

Finding 7's ordinary road: at a Finishing Blow or a victim run out, the stage is written before the death is recorded, and the tracker's reopen (a 120 ms debounce, then the window's close) races the death's row (one chat write, then the GMs' store). Which lands first on a real server was not established; if the reopen wins, Stage 6's tracker has no Silence now. A reading on a table would settle it: after a Finishing Blow, the tracker's footer.

Finding 1's leg with the roller's player away: a GM's own throw goes to resolveOpening through requestOpeningResult's local road (bridge-asks.mjs:46-50), which has no once-only check; whether roll-draw.mjs keeps a record of a GM's own throw that something else would read was not traced.

The roll window an opening invitation opens is Daggerheart's, dressed by roll-dialog.mjs: its own buttons were not read here. The GM's statistic window an opening or a crisis roll waits on (trait-ruling.mjs traitFor) and the GM's side of Take from the Body (handover.mjs lootBody, bridge-runs-records.mjs handleLoot) were not read here either.

murder-rules.mjs was read in the parts that build, wire and handle controls (3053 of 4746 lines). Not read: 1-124, 351-404, 620-659, 1530-2375 (the GM's scoring of a crisis action and its undo), 2466-2861, 2952-3039, 3255-3399. A grep of the whole file for drpgWindow, drpgConfirm and drpgPrompt gives the seven sites read.

Layout was not measured: whether a footer's buttons or a row are clipped at a narrow or short screen in either theme. Only rules that hide (display: none, visibility: hidden, pointer-events: none) were searched, by a script over styles/*.css.

The Event panel's hover texts under Monokuma Legacy: the motive card's and the trial clock's data-tooltip sit in a panel that takes no pointer there (danganronpa.css:10216), so by the stylesheet as read they cannot be hovered, while under Stained Glass they can (stained-glass.css:730). No control is affected and the motive's consequence is printed on the card; whether Foundry's tooltip shows over such an element was not tried.

The body's tile has no control of the module's: it is laid at alpha 0, and the caption on the corpse's token takes no pointer (body-tile.mjs:420-421). Whether Foundry 14 draws a tile at alpha 0 to nobody, a GM included, is the module's own LIVE-E95-01.
